column3: The Hebrew asks briefly whether there is peace; BSB expands this to asking whether Jehu has come in peace.
The Hebrew explicitly says he lifted his face toward the window.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and uses singular “he trampled her”; BSB names Jehu and uses plural “they.”
The Hebrew leaves the entrant unnamed and calls her a king’s daughter in a nominal clause; BSB supplies Jehu and “was.”
The Hebrew leaves the recipient of the report unnamed and names the servant’s hand; BSB supplies Jehu and uses through.
The Hebrew retains the face of the field and calls the remains her corpse; BSB says body lying in the field.
